description: The most popular sport worldwide, known as soccer in some countries, played with a round ball mostly using feet, except for goalkeepers.
A variation of football played on sand, usually with fewer players and adapted rules.
A version of football played in bogs or swamps, requiring extra physical effort.
Football played on ice with or without skates, requiring extra balance and skill.
A variation where elephants are used in place of human players.
A five-a-side version of football played indoors with a smaller, heavier ball.
A variation of football played indoors, often with walls to keep the ball in play.
An indoor football version played in a cage-like structure.
A two-a-side version of football played in an enclosed space.
A tabletop game designed to replicate association football.
A tabletop version of football using miniature figures attached to rotating rods.
A combination of football and pool, played on a giant pool table.
A variation of football for visually impaired players, using a ball with bells inside.
A version of football for athletes with cerebral palsy.
An experimental football game played by three teams on a hexagonal field.
A slower-paced football game designed for older players.
A sport focused on performing tricks and skills with a football.
A table sport using elements of football, played with a curved table.
A fun variation where players move like crabs, using hands and feet.
Football played while encased in a large inflatable bubble (Zorb).
An extreme football variation played with a flaming coconut ball in Indonesia.
A football simulation played by robots.
A unique sport played on the side of a vertical surface.
A form of rugby football that originated from a split in the codes, where teams attempt to carry the ball over the end line while being tackled by the opposition.
A form of rugby football similar to Rugby League but with different rules, such as contested scrums and lineouts.
A variation of Rugby Union with seven players per team, played on a full-size field but with shorter match durations, and now an Olympic sport.
A five-a-side version of rugby played on a smaller field with modified rules.
An indoor version of Rugby Union played on a smaller field, leading to a faster and higher-scoring game.
A variation of Rugby League with nine players per team, played with a focus on speed and open play.
A seven-a-side version of Rugby League played with fewer players and faster gameplay.
A variation of rugby played on sand, typically with fewer players and adapted rules.
A version of rugby played on snow, often in shin-deep conditions, requiring modifications to standard gameplay.
A non-contact version of rugby where players must touch the ball carrier instead of tackling.
A non-contact rugby variant where a Velcro-attached tag is pulled off the ball carrier instead of a tackle.
A rugby adaptation for elderly players and those with limited mobility, played at a walking pace.
A traditional seven-a-side ball game from Manipur, India, similar to rugby but played using a coconut.
A Georgian folk sport that closely resembles rugby, played as a full-contact ball game.
A full-contact sport evolved from rugby, where players aim to get the ball into the opponent's end zone by running or passing. Players wear protective gear, and forward passing is allowed.
A variation of American Football played in Canada with 12 players per team, different field dimensions, and three downs to gain 10 yards.
A smaller team version of American Football designed for schools with fewer students, featuring only six players per team.
A variation of American Football with eight players per team, offering a more open field and faster play.
A version of American Football with nine players per team, balancing elements of traditional and small-team formats.
A non-contact version of American Football where defenders remove a flag or belt from the ball carrier instead of tackling.
A non-contact variation where players only need to touch the ball carrier instead of tackling.
An indoor version of American Football played on a smaller field, leading to a faster-paced and high-scoring game.
A varsity sport in the USA for lightweight players, emphasizing speed and agility.
A variation of football played in kayaks, where players attempt to get a small soft football into the end zone.
A version of football played with a frisbee instead of a ball, blending elements of football and ultimate frisbee.
A variation of American Football played by women wearing lingerie-style uniforms, originally a promotional event now a league sport.
A unique version of American Football where players ride unicycles while playing.
A unique full-contact sport played in Australia with 18 players per team on an oval field, known locally as 'Footy'.
A modified version of Australian Rules Football with nine players per team, divided into forwards, centers, and backs, played on various field sizes.
A version of Nine-a-side Footy developed in the USA as an introductory game leading into full AFL leagues.
A social and inclusive non-contact version of Australian Rules Football, designed for players of all genders, shapes, and sizes.
A traditional Irish sport where players aim to kick or punch a round ball into the net or over the crossbar, using goals similar to rugby but with an attached net.
A game combining elements of Australian Rules Football and Gaelic Football, designed for cross-code competition.
A sport inspired by Australian Rules Football and Rugby Union, played in Samoa.
an indoor court game played with gloves, hitting the ball against the wall.
